items.article_search_text: Formula 1 fans were left star-struck after spotting Mercedes driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Oscar Piastri at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on Monday (Sept 28), ahead of this weekend's race at Sepang International Circuit.Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto was also reportedly spotted, along with engineers and staff from teams including McLaren, Red Bull and Audi.Netizens took to social media to... Formula 1 fans were left star-struck after spotting Mercedes driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Oscar Piastri at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on Monday (Sept 28), ahead of this weekend's race at Sepang International Circuit. Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto was also reportedly spotted, along with engineers and staff from teams including McLaren, Red Bull and Audi. Netizens took to social media to share their excitement, with pictures and videos of the drivers. "Oscar has landed in Malaysia!" wrote laurogeitabat on Threads, adding that the 25-year-old stopped for pictures and autographs. The video, posted on Monday, shows the Australian driver posing for a selfie with a fan before heading towards the airport exit with his entourage. Antonelli was also seen waving at fans and stopping for a photo while manoeuvring his luggage in a separate video posted to Threads by sec_hann28 on Sept 28. The Italian currently leads the Formula One Drivers' Championship with 302 points, while Mercedes teammate George Russell is in second place, with 236 points. The drivers flew into Kuala Lumpur from Baku following Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, where Russell claimed victory ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar. Antonelli finished fifth. "We met Gabriel Bortoleto," Threads user nr.suriana wrote on Monday, sharing a video of the Audi driver noticing them and waving in their direction. Besides the faces of F1, fans also gushed over the engineers and staff members from the various teams. "It's a beautiful night when you accidentally arrived [at] the same time as McLaren, Williams, Haas, Audi, Red Bull engineers and staff," wrote fionanhy on Threads at 3am on Monday with a video of a throng of people waiting with their luggage. She added that the race in Malaysia is "getting real". Threads user f1leaks.my also posted on Sept 28 that engineers and staff from Alpine, Aston Martine and Cadillac were amongst those that had arrived in Kuala Lumpur. The Formula One race at Sepang International Circuit, scheduled for Oct 2 to 4, marks the championship's return to Malaysia for the first time since 2017. Although held in Malaysia, the event will officially be known as the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix after Formula One relocated the race from its original venue amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

items.article_search_text: The McLaren driver explained why he failed to score points at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. McLaren driver Oscar Piastri made a serious mistake late in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix while battling for points.The Australian locked both front wheels simultaneously on lap 40 as he approached Turn 1. The incident occurred while he was trying to defend his position from Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar. Piastri had been running second until that point and had managed to keep Max Verstappen behind him through lap 30.The safety car was deployed after Alex Albon’s crash. Piastri failed to maintain his position after the restart and dropped back following the incident one lap after the second restart, eventually finishing the race in 13th place.Piastri explained his mistake as follows: “It was a bit strange. Both front wheels locked up at once. While defending, I was on a different line from the one I usually use. I don’t know whether I went over a bump, but it came as a surprise to me.”He said the weekend as a whole had been more encouraging than the previous races. Piastri added that he had been able to extract more lap-time performance from the car and had gained a better understanding of the areas in which he needed to improve his driving style.“Apart from one episode in the race, I was closer to the level I expected of myself this weekend. That is more encouraging in this regard. But not getting anything in return for it yet hurts a lot,” he added.Piastri’s 13th-place finish and Lando Norris’ early retirement meant McLaren left Baku without points. The team also suffered an additional setback in its battle with Ferrari for second place in the Constructors’ Championship.The Azerbaijan Grand Prix is held on Baku’s street circuit, where narrow sections and heavy braking zones can make defending positions particularly demanding. In Formula One, a double front-wheel lock-up can cause a driver to miss the corner entry and lose significant time or positions. items.article_search_text: The Azerbaijan GP where Oscar Piastri's title hopes started to sink in 2025 has haunted the Australian again... Oscar Piastri's Baku misery has resurfaced again with the Australian guilty of what a former world champ called a "rookie mistake", blowing the chance of a podium finish while George Russell completed an immaculate lights-to-flag victory in the crashed-marred Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Piastri, whose championship hopes began to crumble last year when he crashed on the tight road circuit with which he's had a "love-hate relationship", this time locked up with third place in his grasp with 10 laps left on Saturday and slid straight into the run-off. By the time he got back on track, he was 15th, his hopes of any points gone, and he ended up 14th, with McLaren suffering double woe after Lando Norris had earlier crashed out, maddened at being the innocent victim in a multiple crash caused by Franco Colapinto. Up ahead, Russell, who led from start to finish and survived the pressure of two restarts under the safety car, held off Max Verstappen in a dramatic finish to win his first race for three months and cut into Mercedes' teammate Kimi Antonelli's championship lead. Russell managed to defend from Verstappen, who charged from eighth through to second, despite his Mercedes losing power in the denouement as Valtteri Bottas's last-lap crash in his Cadillac forced both the leaders to slow as the finish line approached. At the end, Russell had less than two-tenths of a second to spare over his old rival, a margin rather smaller than he'd won his pole by in qualifying. "I lost the boost, I had no power. Thought he was going to get us," a relieved Russell said. Verstappen's Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar was third in a superb return from injury. Antonelli, who'd started 16th after a qualifying crash, ended up battling his way through to fifth, limiting the damage to his title lead as he's still 66 points ahead. But Piastri couldn't hide his disappointment at the miserable conclusion to what had been a weekend when he'd seemingly rekindled his 'love' for the track where he'd won in 2024. On the soft tyres, he'd whipped past Ferrari's Charles Leclerc at the start to grab second place and then held off the challenge of the Red Bulls impressively. But after Alex Albon went into the wall on lap 31 and Piastri found himself on the mediums after everyone pitted under the yellow flag, he was picked off immediately by Verstappen on the restart. Then, with the race having to be restarted again once Colapinto caused the crash which took out both his Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly and Norris, Piastri bemoaned his slide-off error while under pressure from Hadjar. The mistake didn't impress outspoken 1997 world champion Jacques Villeneuve, who told Sky Sports: "It was a rookie mistake. He got caught out, looking in his mirrors, and just completely missed." Piastri's view was, unsurprisingly, different. "I didn't think I braked super-late or super-hard, but just instantly locked both fronts," said the Victorian. "It certainly took me by surprise, "Just a disappointing end to the day. The first half of the race was very strong, so it's a shame not to have anything to show for it." Norris had been left dismayed by his race ending because Colapinto locked up while ploughing recklessly down the inside after the safety-car restart, an error which the Argentine apologised for profusely. Norris, though, muttered darkly: "Just some drivers that shouldn't be in Formula One to be honest." He felt the Argentine should get a one-race ban because "that's not driving that deserves to be in Formula One", but both Verstappen and Russell felt that a suspension would be too harsh. items.article_search_text: The Baku City Circuit’s combination of long straights, heavy braking zones and narrow Old City corners demands precision, commitment and carefully balanced car set-ups, drivers say. The Baku City Circuit’s combination of long straights, heavy braking zones and narrow Old City corners demands precision, commitment and carefully balanced car... Baku’s combination of high-speed straights and tight corners makes it one of Formula 1’s most unusual and demanding venues, Mercedes driver George Russell told Anadolu Agency.McLaren’s Oscar Piastri said the Azerbaijan capital’s street circuit requires “pure commitment”, while circuit designer Carsten Tilke said its character is closely tied to Baku’s historic setting and existing streets.Ahead of Saturday’s 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the drivers and designer described the features that have made the Baku City Circuit one of the sport’s most distinctive venues.The 6.003-kilometre street circuit, which hosted Formula 1 for the first time in 2016, takes cars from one of the calendar’s longest straights into heavy braking zones and the narrow streets surrounding Baku’s Old City. A small error can send a car into the barriers and end a driver’s race.Two contrasting challenges in one lapRussell, who secured pole position in Friday’s qualifying session, said Baku presents “two very different challenges” during a single lap.“You’ve got one of the longest straights of the season where you’re reaching incredibly high speeds, and then you've got the tight, technical sections through the Old City where there's absolutely no margin for error,” he told Anadolu Agency.Russell said the circuit is neither a conventional street track nor a traditional racing venue. Its long straights, heavy braking areas and extremely narrow corners make it “one of the most unusual and demanding events of the year”.The section around the Old City walls is the part drivers most readily associate with Baku, he said, because its tight corners leave almost no room for mistakes.“You need to balance commitment with discipline. In Baku, the walls are always there waiting for you, but if you focus on that too much, you end up driving below the limit,” Russell said. He added that drivers must prepare thoroughly, build confidence in practice and trust their instincts during the race.He also pointed to the contrast between Baku’s modern skyline and historic centre as another feature that sets the circuit apart.Overtaking and set-up compromisesPiastri said Baku differs from many other street circuits because its long straights provide genuine opportunities to overtake.“This presents good opportunities to recover that don’t exist elsewhere,” he told Anadolu Agency. However, low tyre degradation limits the strategic alternatives available to teams, meaning overtaking is often the main way for a driver to regain positions.Although the track changes sharply from ultra-fast sections to the narrow Old City, Piastri said drivers do not necessarily need to adopt a different mindset during each lap. Maintaining concentration, however, becomes even more important.The contrasting high- and low-speed sections also create a difficult engineering compromise between downforce, drag and mechanical grip. Cars built around higher-downforce packages can be competitive at tracks such as Silverstone and Barcelona but may struggle in Baku, where teams generally favour lower downforce to improve straight-line speed.“Like every street circuit, Baku is one that requires pure commitment,” Piastri said, describing the combination of fast sectors and technical corners as a challenge for drivers and engineers, as well as an entertaining spectacle for fans.A circuit shaped by BakuTilke, one of the designers involved in creating the circuit, said the original goal was to make the track inseparable from the city around it.“As a street circuit, the existing road network and city infrastructure naturally defined many of the possibilities and constraints for the layout,” he told Anadolu Agency. The designers identified the streets that could provide the best racing experience and connected them to form a challenging circuit.Baku’s Old City was intended to play a central role from the outset, Tilke said. Its inclusion gave the circuit a distinctive identity and established a strong connection with the capital.He said the contrast between the track’s very fast and extremely narrow sections emerged largely from the existing road network. The challenge was to connect those roads into a coherent racing circuit.A decade after Baku joined the Formula 1 calendar, Tilke said the venue had developed a strong and distinctive identity. While some details could potentially be refined, he argued that any changes should preserve the features that make the circuit recognisable.“Its identity is closely connected to the city, its historic setting and the existing streets,” Tilke said. “Any potential changes should therefore support the circuit’s development without changing what makes it distinctive.” Latest news from Azerbaijan and the world - politics, economy, sports, culture and society

Oscar Piastri acknowledged McLaren had no chance of outpacing George Russell to pole position during qualifying at the Formula 1 Azerbaijan GP, despite finding some ‘surprise’ pace. Piastri will start in third behind Russell and Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc for Saturday’s race in Baku, with teammate and reigning world champion Lando Norris claiming fifth. It’s the sixth time this season the Australian driver has out-qualified Norris for a Grand Prix. Oscar Piastri and Charles Leclerc had no answer for George Russell Piastri welcomes ‘surprise’ McLaren pace The result comes after a tricky start to the weekend for McLaren, who found themselves some way down the leaderboard during the earlier free practice sessions. The team found additional pace during Friday’s qualifying session, but were no match for Russell, whose dominant lap cleared Piastri by more than eight tenths. Piastri, however, was pleased by the result, with the team having brought a significant body package upgrade ahead of the weekend in an attempt to boost its straightline speed. “We found a bit of pace. It's not the first time that's happened to us this year,” he said. “We seem like we're a bit on the back foot through practice. “We've come out in qualifying, and we just find that bit extra. I was pretty surprised to see us one-two after the first lap of Q3, but unfortunately, we had no hope against George. “I'm happy with how the weekend's gone so far. It's never easy around here, especially when it's so gusty like today, so I'm very happy to be back in the top three.” Strong winds in Baku can make it difficult to predict the cars’ balances, particularly in exposed parts of the track. Asked how he manages these challenges, Piastri responded: “Honestly, trying to keep it between the lines, the highway lines down the straights, not easy, especially it always sounds so dull talking about the wind in a Formula 1 car, but even when the walls disappear and you get a bit more open, you really get a massive gust, so it's not easy at all. “There's 30- or 40kph difference sometimes between laps, so you’ve really got to be on your toes and adapt on the fly.” READ MORE -

Although Brown did not confirm that McLaren is preparing to replace either of its current drivers, these comments sparked speculation about who is going to be the driver Verstappen will replace. I feel like I can really race with this guy, because I hate racing against him.”This is significant because Verstappen, 28, has now signed a long-term deal with Red Bull, and Lando Norris is considered the “golden anchor” and extremely protected. Even though Brown did not comment on whom he will replace, that did not stop the fans from starting a whole new online speculation.Lando Norris has become the McLaren Formula 1 Team’s long-term cornerstone after winning his first Drivers’ Championship in 2025. Piastri established himself as a genuine Championship contender and finished third. Both of them won seven races during the last campaign.So until F1 suddenly gives McLaren a third car, somebody is definitely going under the bus.
